To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel recombinant antibody fragment, targeting pathogenic α-syne fibrils, can be efficiently solubilized and purified using mild solubilizers and slow on-column refolded to preserve its secondary structure and bio-activity.
mild solubilisation followed by on column refolding can be used to purify scFvs from IBs.
we have developed a novel method to solubilise and purify a recombinant antibody fragment from inclusion bodies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient protocol to solubilise IBs and the characterization of a novel scFv against α-syn fibrillar aggregates.
a novel approach to purify a recombinant antibody fragment from IBs, and to study its binding characteristics with a pathogenic target.
the development of a new method to purify and characterize the scFv-F antibody fragment from IBs and its potential use in the diagnosis and treatment of synucleinopathes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mild solubilisation followed by slow on column refolding can be utilised as a generalized and efficacious method for hard to pure disease relevant insoluble protein and/or antibody molecules.

the mild solubilisation and on-column refolding protocol can be utilised as a general and efficient method for difficult to purify disease-related insoluble protein and/or antibodies from inclusion bodies (IB) for further structural, biochemical and biophysical characterization.
the mild solubilisation protocol with subsequent slow on-column refold method was successfully employed to obtain the active and soluble scFv-F from IBs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the scFv-F antibody fragment can be expressed in inclusion bodies and solubilized by a mild protocol to obtain active protein that is highly specific towards α-synucleins.
we have demonstrated the utility of a mild solubility protocol for a disease relevant insoluble protein (α-synuclein) as well as a disease relevant antibody (scFv) from IBs.
a novel α-syn specific scFv-F was successfully engineered, expressed and purified.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mild solubilizers such as high pH can be used to preserve protein secondary structures, which is important for maintaining protein bioactivity and stability.
scFv antibodies can be successfully purified from IBs, thus opening the door for their use in immunotherapy.
the mild solubilisation and refolding method described here is a generalized method that can be used to solubilise and refold a wide range of insoluble proteins and antibody molecules from IB.
